sentences.text: Linear and logistic regression are two of many algorithms.

sentences.text: You do not need to master all of them now, but you should know what each one is for, what it is good and bad at, and which one to try first.
sentences.say: You do not need to master all of them now, but you should know what each one is for, what it is good and bad at, and which one to try first.

sentences.text: This chapter is the tour, based on Infinite Codes' 17-minute overview and extended with practical advice.
sentences.say: This chapter is the tour, based on Infinite Codes' 17-minute overview and extended with practical advice.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: Almost every algorithm is either supervised (learn from labels) or unsupervised (find structure).
sentences.say: Almost every algorithm is either supervised (learn from labels) or unsupervised (find structure).

sentences.text: For tables of data, the usual strong choices are random forests and gradient boosting.
sentences.say: For tables of data, the usual strong choices are random forests and gradient boosting.

sentences.text: Start with a simple baseline, then compare.
sentences.say: Start with a simple baseline, then compare.

sentences.text: Some algorithms need scaled features (nearest neighbours, SVM, neural networks, k-means, PCA); trees do not.
sentences.say: Some algorithms need scaled features (nearest neighbours, SVM, neural networks, k-means, PCA); trees do not.

sentences.text: Choose by measuring on held-out data (Chapter 12), not by reputation.

sentences.text: 13.1 Supervised algorithms
sentences.say: 13.1 Supervised algorithms

sentences.text: K-nearest neighbours (KNN).
sentences.say: K-nearest neighbours (KNN).

sentences.text: To predict for a new case, find the K most similar cases in the training data and take the majority vote (classification) or the average (regression).
sentences.say: To predict for a new case, find the K most similar cases in the training data and take the majority vote (classification) or the average (regression).

sentences.text: Analogy: ask the five people who live closest to you which restaurant is good.
sentences.say: Analogy: ask the five people who live closest to you which restaurant is good.

sentences.text: There is no training step at all: the data is the model.
sentences.say: There is no training step at all: the data is the model.

sentences.text: K is a hyperparameter.
sentences.say: K is a hyperparameter.

sentences.text: A small K overfits, because one odd neighbour decides, and a large K underfits.
sentences.say: A small K overfits, because one odd neighbour decides, and a large K underfits.

sentences.text: It needs scaled features, because distance mixes them, and it is slow on big data.
sentences.say: It needs scaled features, because distance mixes them, and it is slow on big data.

sentences.text: Loan: judge a new application like its 5 most similar past ones.
sentences.say: Loan: judge a new application like its 5 most similar past ones.

sentences.text: Support vector machine (SVM).
sentences.say: Support vector machine (SVM).

sentences.text: Draws the boundary between two classes with the widest possible empty margin, like the widest street you can fit between two neighbourhoods.
sentences.say: Draws the boundary between two classes with the widest possible empty margin, like the widest street you can fit between two neighbourhoods.

sentences.text: A trick called a kernel lets the street curve.
sentences.say: A trick called a kernel lets the street curve.

sentences.text: It works well on medium-sized data and needs scaled features.
sentences.say: It works well on medium-sized data and needs scaled features.

sentences.text: Loan: approve or decline from income and debt.
sentences.say: Loan: approve or decline from income and debt.

sentences.text: The video's own example separates cats from elephants by weight and nose length.
sentences.say: The video's own example separates cats from elephants by weight and nose length.

sentences.text: Naive Bayes.
sentences.say: Naive Bayes.

sentences.text: Uses Bayes' theorem (Chapter 15) and naively assumes that features are independent given the class, so it just multiplies simple probabilities.
sentences.say: Uses Bayes' theorem (Chapter 15) and naively assumes that features are independent given the class, so it just multiplies simple probabilities.

sentences.text: The assumption is wrong, but it is fast and works surprisingly well for text.
sentences.say: The assumption is wrong, but it is fast and works surprisingly well for text.

sentences.text: Its probabilities are often poorly calibrated.
sentences.say: Its probabilities are often poorly calibrated.

sentences.text: Loan: sort customer emails into complaints and questions.
sentences.say: Loan: sort customer emails into complaints and questions.

sentences.text: The classic example is the spam filter.
sentences.say: The classic example is the spam filter.

sentences.text: Decision tree.
sentences.say: Decision tree.

sentences.text: A chain of yes or no questions ("credit score below 650? amount above 20,000?"), chosen so that each final leaf is as pure as possible, meaning mostly one class.
sentences.say: A chain of yes or no questions ("credit score below 650? amount above 20,000?"), chosen so that each final leaf is as pure as possible, meaning mostly one class.

sentences.text: Analogy: the game of twenty questions.
sentences.say: Analogy: the game of twenty questions.

sentences.text: It is easy to explain and needs no scaling, but a deep tree memorizes the data (overfits) and changes a lot when the data changes a little.
sentences.say: It is easy to explain and needs no scaling, but a deep tree memorizes the data (overfits) and changes a lot when the data changes a little.

sentences.text: Loan: "credit score below X? amount above Y?"
sentences.say: Loan: "credit score below X? amount above Y?"

sentences.text: The video's example is heart-attack risk.
sentences.say: The video's example is heart-attack risk.

sentences.text: Worked example: Gini impurity.
sentences.say: Worked example: Gini impurity.

sentences.text: The tree needs a score for how mixed a group is.
sentences.say: The tree needs a score for how mixed a group is.

sentences.text: The usual one is Gini impurity: 1 minus the sum of the squared shares of each class.
sentences.say: The usual one is Gini impurity: 1 minus the sum of the squared shares of each class.

sentences.text: Ten offers, 6 accepted and 4 not: 1 - (0.6² + 0.4²) = 0.48.
sentences.say: Ten offers, 6 accepted and 4 not: 1 minus (0.6² + 0.4²) equals 0.48.

sentences.text: A pure group scores 0, and a 50/50 group scores 0.5.
sentences.say: A pure group scores 0, and a 50/50 group scores 0.5.

sentences.text: Now try the question "credit score below 600?".
sentences.say: Now try the question "credit score below 600?".

sentences.text: The left group holds 5 offers, 4 accepted and 1 not: 1 - (0.8² + 0.2²) = 0.32.
sentences.say: The left group holds 5 offers, 4 accepted and 1 not: 1 minus (0.8² + 0.2²) equals 0.32.

sentences.text: The right group holds 5 offers, 2 accepted and 3 not: 1 - (0.4² + 0.6²) = 0.48.
sentences.say: The right group holds 5 offers, 2 accepted and 3 not: 1 minus (0.4² + 0.6²) equals 0.48.

sentences.text: Weighted by size, the two groups score (5/10) x 0.32 + (5/10) x 0.48 = 0.40, so the split gains 0.48 - 0.40 = 0.08.
sentences.say: Weighted by size, the two groups score (5/10) times 0.32 plus (5/10) times 0.48 equals 0.40, so the split gains 0.48 minus 0.40 equals 0.08.

sentences.text: The tree tries every feature and cutoff, keeps the split with the biggest gain, and repeats inside each group.
sentences.say: The tree tries every feature and cutoff, keeps the split with the biggest gain, and repeats inside each group.

sentences.text: This is scikit-learn's default (criterion="gini").
sentences.say: This is scikit-learn's default (criterion="gini").

sentences.text: Random forest.
sentences.say: Random forest.

sentences.text: Many trees, each trained on a random sample of the rows and a random subset of the features, then a vote.
sentences.say: Many trees, each trained on a random sample of the rows and a random subset of the features, then a vote.

sentences.text: Analogy: a hundred doctors, each given a differently redacted copy of the patient file, who vote.
sentences.say: Analogy: a hundred doctors, each given a differently redacted copy of the patient file, who vote.

sentences.text: Each doctor is unreliable alone, but their mistakes differ, so the vote is steady.
sentences.say: Each doctor is unreliable alone, but their mistakes differ, so the vote is steady.

sentences.text: This is bagging, and it mainly cuts variance (Chapter 11).
sentences.say: This is bagging, and it mainly cuts variance (Chapter 11).

sentences.text: Hard to overfit, little tuning, less interpretable than one tree.
sentences.say: Hard to overfit, little tuning, less interpretable than one tree.

sentences.text: Boosting (AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost and relatives).
sentences.say: Boosting (AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost and relatives).

sentences.text: Trees built one after another, each trying to fix the errors of the previous ones.
sentences.say: Trees built one after another, each trying to fix the errors of the previous ones.

sentences.text: Analogy: a tutor who sets the next lesson only on the questions you got wrong.
sentences.say: Analogy: a tutor who sets the next lesson only on the questions you got wrong.

sentences.text: It is often the most accurate method on tables of data, but it overfits more easily than a random forest and trains more slowly.
sentences.say: It is often the most accurate method on tables of data, but it overfits more easily than a random forest and trains more slowly.

sentences.text: Key settings: the number of trees, their depth and the learning rate.
sentences.say: Key settings: the number of trees, their depth and the learning rate.

sentences.text: Loan: the classic tool for default prediction.
sentences.say: Loan: the classic tool for default prediction.

sentences.text: Neural networks.
sentences.say: Neural networks.

sentences.text: Layers of simple units that learn their own features.
sentences.say: Layers of simple units that learn their own features.

sentences.text: 13.2 Unsupervised algorithms
sentences.say: 13.2 Unsupervised algorithms

sentences.text: K-means (clustering).
sentences.say: K-means (clustering).

sentences.text: Pick K centres, assign every point to its nearest centre, move each centre to the middle of its points, and repeat until nothing changes.
sentences.say: Pick K centres, assign every point to its nearest centre, move each centre to the middle of its points, and repeat until nothing changes.

sentences.text: Analogy: choose where to put K pizza shops so that everyone has a shop nearby, then move each shop to the middle of its own customers.
sentences.say: Analogy: choose where to put K pizza shops so that everyone has a shop nearby, then move each shop to the middle of its own customers.

sentences.text: You must choose K (often by trying several and looking for the bend in the error curve), the features must be scaled, and it assumes roundish groups.
sentences.say: You must choose K (often by trying several and looking for the bend in the error curve), the features must be scaled, and it assumes roundish groups.

sentences.text: Loan: customer segments.
sentences.say: Loan: customer segments.

sentences.text: The video's example is emails grouped into three unnamed groups.
sentences.say: The video's example is emails grouped into three unnamed groups.

sentences.text: Hierarchical clustering and DBSCAN.
sentences.say: Hierarchical clustering and DBSCAN.

sentences.text: Hierarchical clustering repeatedly merges the two closest groups and gives a tree of merges (a dendrogram) from which you cut at the level you like.
sentences.say: Hierarchical clustering repeatedly merges the two closest groups and gives a tree of merges (a dendrogram) from which you cut at the level you like.

sentences.text: DBSCAN finds dense regions, can find groups of any shape, and labels isolated points as noise, which also makes it useful for spotting oddities.
sentences.say: DBSCAN finds dense regions, can find groups of any shape, and labels isolated points as noise, which also makes it useful for spotting oddities.

sentences.text: PCA (principal component analysis).
sentences.say: PCA (principal component analysis).

sentences.text: Rotates the axes to point along the directions of greatest variation, then keeps only the first few.
sentences.say: Rotates the axes to point along the directions of greatest variation, then keeps only the first few.

sentences.text: Analogy: the shadow of a 3D object on a wall, from the angle that keeps the most of its shape.
sentences.say: Analogy: the shadow of a 3D object on a wall, from the angle that keeps the most of its shape.

sentences.text: Use it to compress many correlated columns, to draw high-dimensional data in 2D, or to remove redundancy.
sentences.say: Use it to compress many correlated columns, to draw high-dimensional data in 2D, or to remove redundancy.

sentences.text: The new columns are mixtures of the old ones, so they are harder to interpret.
sentences.say: The new columns are mixtures of the old ones, so they are harder to interpret.

sentences.text: Loan: thirty related financial ratios become five components.
sentences.say: Loan: thirty related financial ratios become five components.
